scenes.text: AI coding agents are fast. Run them from a Kanban board, and stories ship three to six times faster than estimated.
But left alone, agents drift. They forget to move cards. They open pull requests for stories nobody claimed. And they finish without logging what the work really cost.
A skill can describe the workflow. It can't enforce it.
Meet pinakas. Greek for board. It makes your Kanban board the single source of truth for human and agent teams.
An agent picks a ready card and claims it. pinakas assigns it, moves it to In Progress, and starts the clock.
Opening a pull request without a claimed card? The hook blocks it. Stopping without actuals? Blocked too.
Every story records the same numbers: duration, tokens, first-pass success, and review findings.
When the pull request opens, the GitHub Action moves the card to review. When it merges, to done, with timing measured from timestamps, not from what the agent reports.
A required check keeps everyone honest. Every pull request closes a card. Every card has actuals. Risky changes need a human approval.
And guardrails fail open. If the board can't be reached, work goes on.
pinakas works with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot today. Codex and GitLab are next.
pinakas. Keep AI coding agents on the board. Open source, on GitHub.
